The code snippet defines a method `extractRTPExtensions` that creates an `ArrayList<RTPExtension>` called `extensionsList`, iterates over media attributes, parses each attribute into an `RTPExtension` object via `parseRTPExtensionAttribute`, and adds the result to the list only if it is not null (line `if (rtpExtension != null) extensionsList.add(rtpExtension);`). The `add` method called is `java.util.ArrayList.add(E)`, which implements `List.add`. The documentation provided lists four exceptions: `UnsupportedOperationException`, `ClassCastException`, `NullPointerException`, and `IllegalArgumentException`. 
- `UnsupportedOperationException`: Thrown if the `add` operation is not supported by the list. `ArrayList` fully supports the `add` operation, so this exception is avoided. 
- `ClassCastException`: Thrown if the class of the element prevents it from being added. `ArrayList` does not enforce type restrictions at runtime (due to type erasure); it accepts any object that is assignment-compatible due to unchecked casts. The element `rtpExtension` is of type `RTPExtension` and the list is declared as `ArrayList<RTPExtension>`, so the cast is safe. Moreover, `ArrayList.add` does not throw `ClassCastException`. Thus it is avoided. 
- `NullPointerException`: Thrown if the element is null and the list does not permit null elements. `ArrayList` permits null elements, so it would not throw this exception even if null were passed. However, the code explicitly checks `if (rtpExtension != null)` before calling `add`, so null is never passed. Thus the exception is avoided. 
- `IllegalArgumentException`: Thrown if some property of the element prevents it from being added. `ArrayList.add` does not throw this exception; it is typically thrown by specialized collections or wrappers. No such restriction exists here, so it is avoided. 

Therefore, all four declared exceptions are avoided in this calling context.

The `IllegalArgumentException` is avoided because `ArrayList.add` does not throw this exception; no element property is checked. Thus there are no un-avoided exceptions.
